blocks.text: The module documentation defines the server proposal flow, fail-closed decisions, idempotency, checkpoints, execution ordering, approvals, interactive tools, audit hygiene, redaction, and headless behavior.
blocks.title: Runner security contract

blocks.text: ApprovalRequest and Choice describe the UI contract. _Outcome and _Call hold validated results and per-call lifecycle state, while _Streamer moves bounded, redacted shell chunks from a worker thread to the event loop.
blocks.title: Call records and stream bridge

blocks.text: ToolRunner stores link, policy, tool, audit, callback, and concurrency dependencies. It also tracks calls, grants, cancellation, checkpoint steps, terminal state, policy denials, and unanswered approvals.
blocks.title: Runner construction and state

blocks.text: Incoming proposals are filtered by run and call id, deduplicated, queued, and processed asynchronously. Observation cancels server-closed or terminal calls; _pipeline then applies policy, approval, audit, checkpoint, execution, and result ordering.
blocks.title: Event intake and call pipeline

blocks.text: These methods read the current policy, validate choices, serialize prompts, remember exact session grants, redact outcomes, dispatch built-in interactive tools, run executors in worker threads, and implement plan_exit.
blocks.title: Policy, approval, and execution gates

blocks.text: Question and task-list helpers convert UI outcomes into fixed model-facing messages or local events. Edited-call notices are bounded and redacted, while checkpointing snapshots a path before mutating execution.
blocks.title: Interactive tools and checkpoints

blocks.text: Approval and result sends handle transport limits without retrying execution. Audit rows omit input and output, restart checks prevent replayed work, and decide/execute expose the same policy and execution gates to headless tooling.
blocks.title: Protocol, audit, and headless answers

gotchas: Denied calls send approval but no tool result.
A missing approval record, checkpoint, or result transport prevents execution.
Session grants are in-memory and exact-input only.
The server's closed-call observation cancels work before a replay can run.

purpose: This module is the security boundary between server-proposed tool calls and local execution. It serializes mutating work, records decisions without sensitive inputs, checkpoints file changes, supports interactive and headless operation, and fails closed when policy, audit, transport, or redaction steps fail.
summary: Mediates proposed device tools through policy, approval, checkpointing, execution, redaction, and protocol responses.
